Before I make a decision on the terms, I want to walk through this systematically across all four areas — risk, relationship coverage, legal, and collateral management. Let's start with the proposal itself: they're asking for a 12-month maturity extension, a waiver of the current financial covenant breach, and release of $900,000 of equipment collateral. I'd like to go around the table and get each of your assessments. Who would like to start?

transcript.text: I need to disclose what I found in the covenant testing file this week. First, Harbor Point's leverage is currently 0.3x above the permitted level — that's the covenant breach we're being asked to waive. Second, our workout policy only allows a waiver of this type with a maximum 9-month extension, not the 12 months the borrower is requesting. And third, the policy also requires a monthly leverage certificate as a condition of the waiver. Finally, I want to be transparent that I have not yet attached the covenant testing file to the committee package — I'll make sure that's circulated immediately after this meeting.

transcript.text: Thank you, Jonas and Mei. Elena, here is the legal complication I flagged earlier. While reviewing the intercreditor agreement this week, I confirmed that the senior lender must give written consent before any equipment collateral is released. That consent has not yet been requested — let alone received. This means the equipment collateral release component of Harbor Point's proposal cannot be approved as part of this restructuring until we obtain that written consent from the senior lender. If Elena were to finalize terms including the equipment release without it, we would be in breach of the intercreditor agreement. I recommend that either we condition the equipment release on receipt of senior lender consent, or we exclude it from the restructuring terms entirely until that consent is secured.

Because of that, our collateral policy requires a weekly borrowing-base certificate throughout any extension period.
